doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Staying in the union and not playing for nothing
summary: He did not hang out for free sessions in New York and transferred his Detroit union card without trouble.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Were you sitting in with any other people in New York or were you doing what most musicians do which is hang out and just get on the hang, get on the circuit?

Well I didn’t hang out that much, I didn’t go out. I knew a lot of guys that went out to Mittens and there were a lot of guys in the Village where you could go. But I didn’t want to play for nothing. (Laughs) I said, “You know I’m in the Union!”
Had you been in the union before?
Yeah, sure in Detroit. I just got transferred.
